::: {.callout-warning}
## Disclaimer 
The dataset used in this analysis is entirely simulated and is not derived from an actual survey or administrative source. The results are intended to illustrate theoretical relationships and statistical procedures rather than to support substantive empirical inference.
:::

## (1) Define a hypothesis and variables

**Dependent Variable (DV)**: Defense Support `defense_support`

**Independent Variable (IV)**: Disinformation Exposure `disinfo_exposure`

**Control Variables**: age `age`, education years `edu_yrs`, party identity `party_id`, and media literacy `media_literacy`

**Hypothesis (H1)**: Higher `disinfo_exposure` is associated with lower `defense_support`, holding controls constant.

### Loading libraries

::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(tidyverse)
library(modelsummary)
library(kableExtra)
```
:::


### Generate a simulated dataset


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(20251216) 
n <- 400 
age <- pmin(pmax(round(rnorm(n, mean = 48, sd=14)), 20), 85) 
edu_yrs <- pmin(pmax(round(rnorm(n, mean = 14, sd=2.5)), 6), 20)
party_id <- sample(c("DPP","KMT","TPP","Other"), 
                   size = n, replace = TRUE, 
                   prob = c(0.35, 0.30, 0.20, 0.15)) 
media_literacy <- pmin(pmax(rnorm(n, mean=4.3, sd = 2.1),0) ,10)
party_shift <- ifelse(party_id == "KMT", 0.8,
               ifelse(party_id == "TPP", -0.4,
               ifelse(party_id == "DPP", -0.6, 0.0)))
disinfo_exposure <- 5 - 0.5 * media_literacy + party_shift + rnorm(n, mean=2.5, sd=1.4)
disinfo_exposure <- pmin(pmax(disinfo_exposure, 0), 10)
party_def <- ifelse(party_id == "DPP", 6,
             ifelse(party_id == "KMT", -4,
             ifelse(party_id == "TPP", -1, 0)))
defense_support <- 60 - 2.4 * disinfo_exposure + 1.2 * media_literacy + 
                  0.08 * edu_yrs - 0.05 * age + party_def + rnorm(n, 0, 10)
defense_support <- pmin(pmax(defense_support, 0), 100)
dat_sim <- data.frame(defense_support, disinfo_exposure, 
                      media_literacy, age, edu_yrs, party_id)
```
:::

## (3) Visualization
I used default functions like `plot` and `hist` for visualization in the begining. I found them lack of customizability so I installed [Tidyverse](https://tidyverse.org/) instead. The Tidyverse includes packages like `ggplot` for better plot designs and `tidyr` for better data forms.



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
dat_long <- dat_sim %>%
  select(defense_support, disinfo_exposure, media_literacy, age) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = everything(),
               names_to = "variable",
               values_to = "value")
ggplot(dat_long, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 25, color = "white", fill = "orange") +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x", ncol = 2,
             labeller = labeller(
               variable = c(
                 defense_support = "Defense support (0–100)",
                 disinfo_exposure = "Disinformation exposure (0–10)",
                 media_literacy  = "Media literacy (0–10)",
                 age             = "Age (years)"
               )
             )) +
  labs(
    title = "Distributions of Key Variables (Simulated Data)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Frequency"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
  )
```

## (4) Model test
Originally, I used default function `summary` to show results of `lm` regression models. However, I was unable to tableize the summerized information. So I (once again) switched to aforementioned `modelsummary` package and queried three linear models.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
models <- list(
  "OLS" = lm(defense_support ~ disinfo_exposure, data = dat_sim),
  "Poission" = glm(defense_support ~ disinfo_exposure, family = poisson, data = dat_sim),
  "OLS with Controls" = lm(defense_support ~ disinfo_exposure + media_literacy + age + edu_yrs + party_id, data = dat_sim)
)
modelsummary(models, stars=TRUE, output="kableExtra")
```
